transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, what brings me in is that I just don't feel real happiness or closeness anymore. It's like I can't. Even when my wife tries to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or... or if something at work goes really well, I just don't feel it.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has it been at least two years, or less than that?
It's been less than two years. Um... this has all been going on since the retrofit accident. That was about one year and seven months ago.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with your wife?

I wouldn't really say I've lost interest. I still try to do my hobbies, and I still make a point to spend time with her. It's not that I don't want to do those things... it's just what I was saying before. I just don't feel the pleasure or happiness when I actually do them.
Would you say that your mood has been persistently low or sad most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't really say I feel sad. It's not a low mood, exactly. Um... I'm not walking around feeling upset or down all day. It's just... like I said before, I just feel kind of blank. I don't really have that sadness, I just don't have the happiness either.
Can you recall if you still react to things that used to bring you joy, like maybe a favorite song or seeing your wife smile? Do those things still have any effect on you emotionally?

Not really, no. That's actually a big part of what brings me in. I just don't feel real happiness or closeness anymore. Even when my wife tries to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or... or if something at work goes really well, it just doesn't have an emotional effect on me. I just don't get that positive reaction anymore.

So you mentioned you don’t feel happiness anymore. Can you tell me if you still show any emotional reaction—like a smile or a feeling of warmth—automatically when something pleasant happens, or does that not happen at all anymore?

No, it really doesn't happen at all anymore. I don't get that automatic feeling of warmth, and I don't really smile at things without having to force it. It's just... flat. Even when something good happens right in front of me, there's just no reaction.
Have you noticed that you no longer react emotionally to things that used to make you feel good, like seeing your wife happy or achieving something at work?

Yeah, like I was just saying, that's exactly what brings me in. I just don't feel real happiness or closeness anymore. Even when my wife tries hard to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or if something goes really well at work... I just don't react to it. The good feelings just aren't there.
Has there been a complete or nearly complete loss of pleasure in all activities that you used to enjoy, not just the ones you mentioned?

Yes, it really is everything. Like I've been saying, that complete lack of feeling is exactly why I made the appointment to come in. I just don't feel any real happiness or closeness anymore, period. It doesn't matter if it's those Sunday routines with my wife, a big success at work, or... or any other hobby I used to have. The enjoyment is just completely gone across the board.
Has this loss of pleasure in activities you used to enjoy stayed constant since the accident, or have there been times when you felt some happiness or enjoyment again, even briefly?
It's been pretty constant. I mean, since the accident, I haven't really had any moments where the enjoyment came back, even for a little bit. It's just been this steady... nothingness the whole time.
